benches.title: Real bugs in famous Python projects
benches.blurb: 30 everyday bug fixes from Django, SymPy, Sphinx, scikit-learn and friends (SWE-bench Verified, quick-fix tier). Every task proven fixable first; every fix graded by the official checker.
benches.takeaway: Both sides fixed most of these — the plain agent 20 of 30, Razor 15 of 30. The difference is the bill: Razor used 1.6495× the tokens.

benches.title: Big Go projects whose tests run
benches.blurb: 8 tasks in Caddy and Hugo — large codebases whose test suites run on the machine, so Razor can check its own work as it goes.
benches.takeaway: The plain agent solved none of the eight and burned ~195k tokens per task exploring. Razor solved two at about 60% of the tokens — and its peak context was a third of the agent's.

benches.title: Small JS/Go projects, hidden tests
benches.blurb: 23 tasks from Preact, Axios, Gin and Vue. The grading tests stay hidden until the end, so Razor's checker is partly blind on this set.
benches.takeaway: Honest result: the plain agent wins on correctness here (7 vs 5). Razor used about the same tokens overall and kept a much smaller peak context (9.4k vs 14.1k tokens).
